about: Touched-path to test-suite map, read by `botq test-map`. First matching rule wins. `tests: []` means consciously untested and carries its why. Commands run from the repo root; lint with `botq test-map --check`.

rules.why: the standalone receiver has its own lockfile, storage and relay tests
editing the map re-lints its own completeness

tests: nix-shell --run 'shellcheck art/ask.sh art/tests/ask.sh && art/tests/ask.sh && cargo test ask_sh -- --test-threads=2 && cargo test direct_sh -- --test-threads=2'
rules.why: the shared runner passes the directive model explicitly and accepts only successful calls with matching transcript models
the recorded image call supplies both caption and input hashes; mismatched attachments must fail before a record is replaced
critic round renders and their score record are inspected together on the stitched proof
visual proof assets are inspected at their native dimensions
source figures are inspected at their native dimensions

tests: nix-shell --run 'shellcheck art/symbols/gen.sh art/overlay/*.sh && art/symbols/gen.sh && cargo test every_symbol_letter_matches_its_binding_and_shift_state && cargo test every_instruction_symbol_is_transparent_at_all_four_shipped_size_corners && cargo test every_display_site_uses_one_renderer_and_exposes_all_four_instruction_symbol_corners && git diff --exit-code -- art/symbols/*.png proofs/tape-case-73.png'
rules.why: one vector source regenerates every symbol and its shipped-size proof; runtime displays place those same alpha-blended textures
direct.sh writes every painted prompt; the stub-codex test runs the script
every shipped texture must keep the prompt that painted it beside it

the machine textures are painted by ziral --gen through paint.sh, their prompts written through direct.sh and their candidates judged through ask.sh; the tests check the shipped scaffolds, prompts, kept candidates, maps and keys against the manifest
the art scripts drive the image tool and the shot renderer; shellcheck is the one static check they have
art direction documents and raster assets; the scripts among them have their own rule above

tests: nix-shell --run 'CC_wasm32_unknown_unknown=clang NIX_HARDENING_ENABLE= cargo clippy --manifest-path web/transport/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- --deny warnings'
rules.why: running the web build is the only thing that compiles the wasm module and checks the wasm-bindgen pin; the frame-budget benchmark runs the busy scene on every target
GitHub is the only runner; the push that lands a workflow is the run that checks it
a parse catches syntax; a build inside the shell catches a missing package; the compiler and browser it pins move frame times, so the frame-budget benchmark runs too
a shader only compiles when a scene is drawn; the proof shot draws lit machines at two turns and fails on a shader error; the frame-budget benchmark runs the busy scene on every target
one crate, one suite; two test threads because the box hangs cargo test under contention; the frame-budget benchmark runs the busy scene on every target
